Definition: from G2596 and the base of G939; to descend (literally or figuratively):--come (get, go, step) down, fall (down).
BiblicalUsage: To come down is what the Son of Man did from heaven, what the Spirit did like a dove at the Jordan, and what Philip did into the water with the Ethiopian. The word carries the whole movement of God toward us and of His people toward one another, down from the heights to where the need is. No one ascends into heaven but He who first descended, and that descent is the shape of the gospel.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the gospel moves downward before it moves upward, because God came down to us before He asks us to rise to Him. I hold that every baptism and every act of coming alongside someone is a small copy of that first great descent.
